sources.title: Find a planning application
sources.verified_claim: Enfield's planning register publishes valid applications and links current weekly new applications and appeals; missing fees or information prevent validation, and decision notices/officer reports are available once issued.

sources.title: Planning appeals
sources.verified_claim: Havering explains statutory appeal routes and states its online appeals database is live and includes appeal decisions; an appeal route does not imply a sample parcel has an appeal or favourable outcome.

sources.title: Planning application decision search
sources.verified_claim: Havering's decision search covers decisions since 1990 and can show conditions, refusal reasons and decision notices for decisions since January 2003; it is a traceability tool rather than parcel evidence by itself.

sources.title: Advice on providing supporting information
sources.verified_claim: Havering notes planning applications may require supporting documents under national policy, the London Plan and the Havering Local Plan, including a Health Impact Assessment for relevant schemes; requirements depend on proposal facts.

sources.title: Search and comment on applications
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth's database contains applications from 1986 onward with decision notices and newer plans, but the council explicitly warns the database is incomplete and is not a substitute for a formal land-charge search.

sources.title: Find out which planning constraints affect your property
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth directs users to land-charge searches, the planning database and Local Plan policies map to identify property constraints and warns that historic permission conditions can also restrict future development.

sources.title: Appeal a planning decision
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth describes appeal rights, time limits and the Planning Inspectorate route; the existence of an appeal process is not evidence that a sample parcel is under appeal or will succeed.

sources.title: Planning enforcement appeals
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth confirms statutory rights to appeal enforcement notices and notes the process can often take up to a year; enforcement status must be established from site-specific records.
